'''Birgitte Kiær Ahring''' (born July 22, 1953) is a Danish [[biologist]] and researcher in [[biofuel]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Birgitte Ahring {{!}} WSU Voiland School Faculty {{!}} Voiland School of Chemical Engineering and Bioengineering {{!}} Washington State University|url=https://voiland.wsu.edu/faculty-staff/birgitte-ahring/|access-date=May 27, 2020|language=en-US}}</ref> Since 2008, she has been employed as a professor at the Department of Chemistry and Bioscience at [[Aalborg University Copenhagen]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Birgitte Kiær Ahring|url=https://vbn.aau.dk/en/persons/117312|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=Aalborg University's Research Portal|language=en|archive-date=September 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921043615/https://vbn.aau.dk/en/persons/117312|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
Ahring graduated as cand.scient. in [[biology]] at [[University of Copenhagen|Copenhagen University]] in 1982. In 1986, she acquired a PhD in [[microbiology]], also from Copenhagen University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ABIC 2010 – Saskatoon, Canada – Agricultural Biotechnology for a competitive and sustainable future|url=http://www.abic.ca/abic2010/html/speakers/birgitte_ahring.html|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=abic.ca|archive-date=May 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160512023855/http://www.abic.ca/abic2010/html/speakers/birgitte_ahring.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
 
== Career ==
In 1986, Ahring became head-scientist at ‘The Nordic Council of Ministers’ [[biofuel]] [[research program]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ABIC 2010 – Saskatoon, Canada – Agricultural Biotechnology for a competitive and sustainable future|url=http://www.abic.ca/abic2010/html/speakers/birgitte_ahring.html|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=abic.ca|archive-date=May 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160512023855/http://www.abic.ca/abic2010/html/speakers/birgitte_ahring.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Also, she was employed at the [[Technical University of Denmark|Technical Folk High School of Denmark]] the same year.
 
Ahring started working as an [[Environmental consulting|environmental consultant]] at the United Nations (UN) focusing on Africa and Asia in 1992. The following year, in 1993, she was employed as a lecturer in [[environmental engineering]] at [[Technical University of Denmark]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=DTU-professor modtager Carl Bros Inspirationspris 2006 – DTU|url=https://www.dtu.dk/Nyheder/2006/11/DTU-professor-modtager-Carl-Bros-Inspirationspris-2006|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=dtu.dk|language=da}}</ref>
 
In 1997, she started working as a professor in [[environmental engineering]] at [[University of California]], Los Angeles, US, and at the same time worked at the research center, [[BioCentrum-DTU (BIC)|Biocentrum]], at the Technical University of Denmark.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Birgitte Ahring {{!}} NARA {{!}} Washington State University|url=https://nararenewables.org/member/birgitte-ahring/|access-date=May 27, 2020|language=en-US}}</ref>
 
In 2004, Ahring became the leader of the Danish Center for Biofuels. Later, in 2006, she became the chief executive and [[Ownership|owner]] of the company, Biogasol. Simultaneously, she started leading the Maxifuel project at the Technical University of Denmark.<ref>{{Cite web|title=MaxiFuels bringer Danmark i front inden for bioethanol – DTU|url=https://www.dtu.dk/nyheder/2006/09/maxifuels-bringer-danmark-i-front-inden-for-bioethanol?id=e8fcc106-e3eb-4b33-8cc5-bd0ec1826d8d|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=dtu.dk|language=da}}</ref>
 
As part of a collaboration between [[Washington State University]] and Aalborg University to develop a new type of [[biofuel]], Ahring was employed as the director of both [[Research institute|research centres]], in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AAU ansætter professor Birgitte Ahring|url=https://vbn.aau.dk/en/clippings/aau-ans%C3%A6tter-professor-birgitte-ahring|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=Aalborg University's Research Portal|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Joshi|first=Pratik|date=June 29, 2008|title=Biofuels research advanced by WSU|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/biofuels-research-advanced-by-wsu/|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=The Seattle Times|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Industrial Biotechnology and Bioprocessing (CPD Credits) is on Aug 16 2018 at COPENHAGEN|url=https://industrial-biotechnology.alliedacademies.com/|access-date=May 27, 2020|website=Allied Academies Conference}}</ref>
